controlled_change: Bounded native state-only K/V/index catch-up, grouping at most four corrected rows. Full-layer priming and all trained proposal forward arithmetic remain unchanged.
correctness: Independent 22-boundary CPU fixture passes; full versus state-only private state is byte-identical for full and proper prefixes with no expert cache access. Joint forced-rejection boundaries and all future timing proposals/target state compare exactly. Offline audits and 20 focused tests pass.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Reduce catch-up work at the same 12GiB budget, 1460 target slots and 32 draft slots; count complete decode wall time.
hypothesis: Updating only private attention state during target-aligned MTP catch-up avoids discarded computation without changing proposals or target output.
limitations: Compression-disturbed timing establishes neither a speed gain nor a regression. Five alternating pairs were not reached.
The earlier 4.7904 real-draft screen is separate evidence, not a control pooled into this experiment.
Short 72-token prompt and 16-token continuation only; long contexts, sustained sessions, tool workflows and non-greedy sampling remain unqualified. Production is unchanged.
outcome: Fresh timing stops at the first memory gate: clean control 4.841001 tokens/s; candidate 4.319057 tokens/s with 53.859MiB peak compression and 73 decompressions, unchanged swap. Zero usable pairs. The candidate numerical validation also had 76.219MiB peak compression. Original reports remain resource_blocked; no historical timings pooled.
smallest_experiment: After a material resource change, collect one clean full-layer versus state-only pair under the same budget. Separately reduce target verification latency; eliminating all catch-up from the clean 4.7904 result still leaves about 202.65ms/token.
